analysis.title: Wall Street just dumped everything right before the next big squeeze (Buy high, sell low)
key_insights: NDX futures printed an unusual intraday hammer candle after the latest selloff. TME reads it as sellers losing control and selling pressure being absorbed, similar to the inverted hammer at the April lows. It says confirmation is needed before a squeeze could turn violent.

SOX has fallen sharply over the past few sessions and is extremely oversold. It has reached the lower boundary of its trading range, which has held on numerous occasions, and is testing its longer-term trend line.

Goldman's Lin reports aggressive global equity selling yesterday, with net flows at -2.1 standard deviations. Long sales outpaced short sales by roughly 3 to 1, which points to outright risk reduction.

The US accounted for 66% of global net selling, led by tech. Korea and Taiwan also saw heavy liquidation. Global AI stocks had their second-largest net selling in a year (-2.8 Z-score). Investors are dumping longs rather than adding shorts.
Hedge funds have net sold global AI stocks for five consecutive sessions. Per Goldman, cumulative hedge fund net buying in the sector since the start of 2025 has been completely reversed.

Hedge fund net allocation to global AI stocks fell to 26.1% from 31.7% at the June peak, now at the 49th percentile over the past year. The aggregate long/short ratio dropped from 4.34 to 3.27, the 7th percentile over the past year. Positioning has been substantially cleaned up.
KOSPI is at its most oversold level since October 2022.

Leopold reportedly bought CoreWeave and other AI-related calls in early September, weeks before the latest selloff. The CRWV November $95 call fell from a high of $18 to about $1 since September 8. TME has not established which specific options were bought, but the contract has substantial open interest.

TME suggests the options unwind may have amplified the selloff. Dealers who bought delta to hedge call exposure may have been forced to sell as the calls lost value, adding pressure to the underlying stocks.

DRAM has fallen back to the Leopold lows, and CRWV's RSI has returned to levels last seen during the initial selloff. TME asks whether positioning washed out, options crushed and deeply oversold technicals make this a second chance.
The Russell is trading at deeply oversold levels. TME says oversold alone is not a strategy but several factors could set up a short-term reversal.

Since July, CFTC data show a positive short-term correlation between changes in Russell 2000 hedge fund short positioning and CDX high-yield spreads. Hedge funds added Russell shorts as credit conditions deteriorated. With short positioning now very large, the potential for a sharp short-covering rally is rising.
Risk management note: Paul Tudor Jones is quoted as saying 'Nothing good happens below the 200-day moving average.' TME's point is to cut risk early and stay in the game.

sector_views.rationale: SOX is extremely oversold at the lower boundary of its trading range and a longer-term trend line. TME asks whether it is time to nibble, without a firm call.
Russell is deeply oversold with heavily crowded hedge fund shorts, which raises short-covering rally potential. TME says buying on oversold alone is not a strategy.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is washed out (AI long/short ratio at the 7th percentile, hedge funds unwound all 2025 AI buying), the NDX hammer suggests sellers are losing control, and SOX sits at range support and trend line. Heavily crowded Russell shorts raise short-covering potential.
tension_points.bear_case: Selling was outright long liquidation (long sales about 3x short sales), the hammer is not confirmation on its own, and oversold is not a strategy. Options unwinds and dealer hedging may add further pressure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break below the lower boundary of the SOX trading range and its longer-term trend line, or no confirmation following the NDX hammer.
